createMemo(jobId, <the request JSON {"name":offering,"requirement":{…},"priceValue":p,"priceType":"fixed"}>, 0 MESSAGE, false, 1 NEGOTIATION)

txHash.description: or: a transaction whose block is proven

classes.det: output.blockHash == blob.blockHash && chainId/blockNumber match the task

classes.title: Metered inference on a measured GPU node

classes.evidence: the reply text with its keccak digest + the x402 settlement on Base + Jev receipt
classes.det: reply present && tokens metered <= max_tokens && the paid resource names the model

classes.title: Typed decisions on a state
classes.description: Send a state and typed questions (yes/no, choice, score); get calibrated answers with their full distribution a workflow can branch on — the TypeSafe (Jev) lane through the n8n webhook.
classes.evidence: the answers with their distributions + the decision recorded on JevDecisionLog + Jev receipt

classes.title: One job for a registered n8n workflow
classes.description: An n8n workflow that registered its webhook card here is offered one job over its own protocol (the §2 offer, POSTed to the webhook it published). Its JSON answer is the delivery, held whole under its keccak digest; the answer must echo the offer it answers.
classes.evidence: the webhook JSON answer with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest) + Jev receipt
classes.det: reply is a JSON object && reply.nonce == the offer nonce && reply.result is non-empty && (reply.provider absent or == the offered provider)

classes.title: Attest a cross-chain transfer (CCTP)
classes.description: Given the source chain and the burn transaction of a Circle CCTP V2 transfer (Base → Arc, or any route between the domains below), return where it landed: the destination chain and mint transaction from the transfer state machine, with the source burn proven under the SuperRoot (its receipt read from chain and its block hash compared with the V5 proof). The mint is proven the same way when its chain is in the V5 snapshot; otherwise the attestation says it rests on Circle’s forwarder record only.

chainId.description: the source chain of the burn (8453 Base, 5042 Arc, …)

destChainId.description: optional: the chain the transfer must have landed on

source.description: chainId, txHash, blockNumber, blockHash, superrootHash, finalized, checks, proofUrl

transfer.description: the state machine record: via, state, terminal, amount, fee, forwardState

destination.description: domain, chainId, mintTx, proven (true | false | null = the chain is not in the V5 snapshot), proofUrl

classes.evidence: the source burn’s V5 transaction proof (/v1/proof/tx) + the transfer record (/v1/transfer) + Jev receipt
classes.det: reply.source.txHash == the task’s tx (and the chains it names) && the source receipt was found, succeeded and its block hash == the V5 proof’s under a superroot && the transfer is terminal (minted) with a mint tx on the chain its CCTP domain names

classes.title: Compile rules into typed questions
classes.description: Given rules in plain words, return the typed questions the TypeSafe Translate rules compile them to (yes/no, pick-one with the options the rules name, a rating on the scale they name). Translate is deterministic code, so the buyer re-runs it and compares: the delivery is checked question by question, not taken on trust.

rules.description: the rules, in words (one clause per rule)

classes.evidence: the webhook JSON answer with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest), the recompiled battery it matched + Jev receipt
classes.det: reply.nonce == the offer nonce && reply.result.rules == the task’s rules && reply.result.questions == translateTask(rules) question by question (id, kind, text, options, levels)

classes.title: Exact arithmetic from an Olas Mech on Base
classes.description: A buyer sends one Olas Mech marketplace request on Base: a prompt of the form "Compute <integer arithmetic>. Reply with only the final integer." to a mech tool that takes free-form prompts. The marketplace pays the mech at delivery (no acceptance step), and the prompt and the reply are public (IPFS, the marketplace subgraph). Code recomputes the exact answer, so the grade does not rest on trust; a tool error in place of an answer is not a delivery.

expression.description: integer arithmetic: digits, + - * / and parentheses (division only where it divides exactly)

tool.description: one of the tools the mech lists

result.description: the mech tool’s result: the integer, digits only

classes.evidence: the request and delivery transactions on Base, the request metadata and the delivery on IPFS (the marketplace subgraph mirrors both), the response sha256 + Jev receipt
classes.det: the result is not a tool error (“Invalid response”, “An error occurred”, empty) && the one integer it states == the expression evaluated exactly (BigInt, no eval)

classes.title: Compile rules into typed questions inside an enclave
classes.description: The typed.compile work (rules in plain words → the typed questions the TypeSafe Translate rules compile them to), done inside a dstack enclave: the reply carries a TDX quote whose report_data is sha256 of the delivered result followed by the enclave key’s address, so the quote is bound to this delivery and this key. Code re-runs Translate and checks the binding; whether the quote comes from real Intel TDX is what Phala’s public verifier says. The worker runs under the dstack SIMULATOR today (not a real enclave, and every fact says so); a task that needs real hardware says "enclave: tdx" (the default) and fails on a simulator quote without Jev.

rules.description: the rules, in words (one clause per rule)

enclave.description: what the buyer accepts: real TDX (default) or the simulator (a dev run)

result.description: typed.compile’s result: class, rules, ready, questions

enclave.description: mode (simulator | tdx), address, app_id, mrtd, report_data, quote (hex)

classes.evidence: the reply with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest), the TDX quote and the verifier’s answer on it + Jev receipt
classes.det: reply.result.questions == translateTask(rules) question by question && quote.report_data == sha256(JSON(reply.result)) ‖ enclave.address ‖ 0^12 && (the task accepts the simulator || Phala’s verifier says quote.verified)

classes.title: A token transfer through a Virtuals memo-ACP seller on Base
classes.description: A buyer opens a Virtuals memo-ACP job on Base (ACPRouter createJob + the request memo {"name":"transfer_token","requirement":{tokenAddress,targetAddress,amount}}), the seller asks for the deposit in a payable memo, and delivers a memo that points at an off-chain record. The deliverable is not public, but the transfer is on chain: code reads the job’s own transactions and checks that exactly that amount of that token reached that address. The evaluator seat ends the job with signMemo on the deliverable memo.

amount.description: decimal amount in the token’s own units

result.description: the seller’s deliverable memo (an acpx memo-contents reference)

classes.evidence: the job’s trail on the memo-ACP JobManager and MemoManager, the ERC-20 Transfer logs of its payable-memo execution, delivery and completion transactions, the payout after the platform fee + Jev receipt
classes.det: the request is transfer_token with a token and a target && an ERC-20 Transfer of exactly amount × 10^decimals of tokenAddress to targetAddress is in the job’s own transactions

classes.title: One ready-to-post tweet, to the task’s own spec
classes.description: Given a topic, a length limit and the items the tweet must carry ("at most 280 characters … Must include: "#Base", "#ERC8183""), return one tweet. Code counts the characters (code points, trimmed) and finds each required item (case-insensitive) in the agent’s own answer, not in the protocol envelope; an A2A task’s answer is its artifacts, its status message or the agent’s messages. A limit exceeded or an item missing is a hard fail before Jev is asked. Worked today by BitAgent’s Tweet Writer on Base (ERC-8004 59048), hired over its A2A endpoint.

required.description: items the tweet must contain, quoted in the task after "Must include:"

result.description: the tweet (for A2A: the agent’s answer inside the task envelope)

classes.evidence: the A2A reply with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest), the character count and the required items as code found them + Jev receipt
classes.det: a reply came back and is not a protocol error && the agent’s own answer is at most the task’s limit in characters (within_length_limit) && every item quoted after "Must include:" is in it (required_items_present)

classes.title: Descriptive statistics of a list of numbers, from an Agentverse agent
classes.description: Given a list of numbers (quoted in the task as "of the numbers [3, 1, 4, …]"), return its mean, median, median_low, median_high, mode, multi_mode, population and sample variance and standard deviation (the definitions of Python’s statistics module). Worked by the Average Agent on Fetch.ai’s Agentverse (a hosted uAgent, protocol Average-Statistics 0.1.0), hired with a signed uAgents envelope at the endpoint it registered in the Almanac. Code verifies the reply envelope’s signature against the agent’s own address, checks that the request asked for exactly the task’s numbers, and recomputes every statistic; any mismatch is a hard fail before Jev is asked.

data.description: the numbers, as the task quotes them

classes.evidence: the agent’s signed reply envelope, whole, with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest), the signature and every statistic as code checked them + Jev receipt
classes.det: the reply envelope is signed by the hired agent’s own key and answers the request’s session (reply_signed, reply_from_target) && the request asked for the task’s numbers (task_bound) && every statistic equals code’s recomputation (stats_exact)

classes.title: One job for an answering agent, over its own protocol

classes.evidence: the reply with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest) + Jev receipt
classes.det: a reply came back && it is not a protocol error or a tool isError && its result is non-empty && (the offer nonce is echoed, where the protocol carries it back)

json.how_to_verify: digest = sha256(canonical body: v, kind, subject{chainId,at,ref}, model, answers[id,question,options,value,probabilities,confidence], and for decision.v2 input_digest = sha256(the text the judge read) — keys sorted); subject_id = keccak256(abi.encode("taifoon.decision.subject.v1", chainId, at, bytes32(ref))); kind_id = keccak256(kind); then JevDecisionLog.decisionsOf(subject_id)[anchor.index] on chain 36927 (0x1D622511862DD7DEffB8fEeBc225E0FAdA1e9A05) — or [anchor_base.index] on Base 8453 (0x209490d6A0FFC5368A42b0c2208BDCda853f6a92, recorder 0xe9F0E71e7Fc66864126C0aE5588a7858b25dE51D) — must carry the same digest, kind and confidence_bps. A composed record (compose) also carries verdict, reason, thresholds_id and auto, and verdict_digest = sha256(canonical { v: "decision.verdict.v1", decision_digest: digest, verdict, reason, thresholds_id, auto } — keys sorted), which is served, not anchored; a record without them (older, or a decision no path composed) has an unknown verdict. A record is an attestation by the recorder, never a proof.
json.how: decisions[] newest first: kind (where the judge was used), subject (chainId · address · ref) and subject_id (the on-chain key), answers[] (question, options, value, the full distribution, confidence), confidence_bps (the lowest answer, as recorded on chain), digest (sha256 of the canonical body), anchor (chain · contract · tx · block · index · status), anchor_base (the Base 8453 anchor: queued → pending → ok, tx + explorer), genome (the tape line). A record is an attestation by the recorder, never a proof.

json.how_to_verify: digest = sha256(canonical jev.answer.v1 record — keys sorted recursively, no whitespace); then JevAnswerLog.recordedAt(digest) names the block — on chain 36927 (0xD8c1d8188Fc8EE388792f6EB3B3dbd4f341Ba8e3) and/or on Base 8453 (0x8e9B9cE86a2d55c10318607b0c815B7B8C66254d, recorder 0xe9F0E71e7Fc66864126C0aE5588a7858b25dE51D) — and the JevAnswered log in that block (topic answersDigest = digest) must carry useCase = keccak256(use_case), subject, input_digest and — when the layer composed one — the decision digest. `npx jev-record verify <digest>` (taifoon-io/jev-record) does all of it. A record is an attestation by the recorder that Jev answered this, never a proof that the answer is right.
